name: Implementation Layer Boundaries

checks.check: Where the adopted architecture separates domain/core from I/O, preserve that boundary; report concrete policy/I/O coupling rather than requiring a new layer taxonomy.
Adapters own external protocol/I/O details; business policy has an explicit owner and must not be silently duplicated in integrations.
Use-case coordination has a clear owner; entry surfaces/adapters must not duplicate or obscure workflow policy.
Entry surfaces delegate complex workflow policy to its owner; identify responsibility mixing rather than using a handler line-count limit.
Workers/execution units have scoped responsibilities and predictable side-effect handling; they may execute assigned business rules but do not self-approve or own another component’s approval truth.
Projections/read models do not mutate authority state or become hidden truth
Config/env access and validation have clear owners; avoid repeated reads of the same setting deep in business logic with inconsistent meaning.
Validation exists at mutation boundaries; expected vs unexpected errors are separated
Read paths and write/mutation paths are distinguishable (not collapsed into a single ambiguous helper)
Type contracts remain explicit across layers; untrusted/unknown input is validated before it is relied on, and escape types do not replace a known contract.
External I/O stays with its declared owner under the adopted architecture; preserve authority and side-effect boundaries without requiring every project to add adapters.
Write/read boundary payload must be explicit, stable, verifiable — mutation inputs and query outputs have defined shapes, not ad-hoc objects
Action/mutation naming reflects business intent — names describe what the business operation does, not implementation mechanics (e.g., `approveOrder` not `updateRow`)
Expected failures have a stable structured contract (including typed exceptions where appropriate), not unclassified raw exceptions or ad-hoc strings.
Critical UI interactions have stable accessible-role/label or test-selector contracts; avoid accidental coupling to cosmetic classes or DOM layout.
DevX hygiene subjective: function name 與 observable side effect 一致（R-NAME-BEHAVIOR per §15.1）
DevX hygiene subjective: 同一 function 混雜唔同抽象責任，令理解或修改一條行為要同時處理無關細節時，指出具體成本；唔以層數判錯。
DevX hygiene subjective: shared mutable state edge case 超出 mechanical lint 偵測範圍（R-SHARED-MUTABLE subjective edge per §15.1）
Complex core logic is extractable from framework surfaces.
Config may validate and resolve declared settings; it must not hide workflow execution, approval decisions or undeclared business policy.
Domain vocabulary is not polluted by transport or adapter naming, and the domain renders no transport output.
Projection failure must respect the declared transaction boundary and must not corrupt authoritative state; explicitly required atomic projection/write coupling remains enforceable.
Ops/runtime assets have clear ownership: scheduler execution metadata may be authoritative for job execution, but must not silently replace product/workflow truth.
Transport parsing and decision-making have clear owners; input parsing must not silently embed workflow or approval policy outside its authorized owner.
Multi-step operations stay atomic, or document the compensating action.
Objects returned to a pool or cache are clean; reset or invalidation happens at the right boundary.
Substitute detection by eye: self-defined schema fields replacing framework templates, and a harness that runs the orchestration shell while swapping out the mechanism actually at risk.

anti_patterns: Folder names treated as architecture instead of actual responsibility boundaries
Direct I/O violates the project’s adopted pure-domain boundary
Adapters carrying business policy or redefining truth
Route/action/handler becoming a "god object" with thick orchestration
Workers silently take over another component’s truth or approve their own actions
Self-HTTP hops where direct in-process calls are appropriate
Sheet/bot/temp file becoming hidden truth — spreadsheets, chat bots, or temp files silently become the system's actual source of truth instead of the designated authority store
Provider response shape silently replaces the declared business contract or is mistaken for authoritative persisted state

Signature changes without call-site audit — required kwarg added to function signature but callers not enumerated and updated (typical: cold paths like worker handlers / error branches / legacy adapters missed; see IMPLEMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINE §5A.1 Signature Evolution)
why: Review guidance, not an enforced checker or proof of review completion. Apply each question to this repo’s actual scope and architecture; state when it does not apply. Source names and R-/PL- identifiers are historical attribution, not required files in the adopter. Historical measurements below describe the recorded experiment, not a new measurement.
